sentences.text: This woman is famous for cruelty, and the Bible may say the exact opposite.
This is Job Derided, painted by Gaspare Traversi, an Italian Rococo painter.
For centuries, Job's wife has been read as the villain of his story.
The theologian Abraham Kuyper even called her Satan's instrument for torturing Job.
And the picture seems to agree.
Her mouth is open at his ear, and her finger points at him.
Her brow is tight with worry.
According to the Book of Job, she asked if he still held fast to his integrity.
And the word translated as curse actually means bless.
The scholar Ilana Pardes calls her a victim of the same divine tests.
She's a second victim of the same test.
So is she mocking him, or the only one telling him the truth?

meta.title: The wife of Job was not what you were told
meta.description: Job Derided is an early work by the Italian Rococo painter Gaspare Traversi, now in the National Museum in Warsaw. Job's wife is usually read as a villain, but the Hebrew word translated as curse literally means bless.
